q: The prototyping model is most appropriate when
options: The requirements are completely known and frozen
The system is a purely computational batch program
The customer's requirements are unclear or incomplete
The project has no user interface
exp: Prototypes help users and developers clarify vague or incomplete requirements through early feedback.

q: Which of the following should NOT be included in a Software Requirements Specification?
options: Choice of algorithms and design/implementation details
exp: An SRS states what the system must do, not how; design and implementation decisions belong to the design documents (IEEE 830).

q: In structured design, the fan-out of a module is
options: The number of modules directly called by it
The number of modules that call it
The number of lines of code it contains
The number of parameters passed to it
exp: Fan-out counts subordinate modules invoked by a module; fan-in counts its callers.

q: Bottom-up integration testing requires the use of
exp: In bottom-up integration, lower-level modules are tested first, so drivers are needed to simulate the higher-level callers.

q: In Function Point Analysis, the Complexity Adjustment Factor (0.65 + 0.01 × ΣFi, with 14 factors each rated 0 to 5) has a maximum value of
According to Lehman's laws of software evolution, a program used in a real-world environment must continually be adapted or it becomes progressively less useful. This is the law of
exp: The law of Continuing Change states that E-type systems must be continually adapted to remain satisfactory.

q: In MoSCoW requirements prioritisation, the letter "W" stands for:
exp: MoSCoW = Must have, Should have, Could have, Won't have this time.

q: Brooks' law states that
options: Software complexity grows exponentially with lines of code
Project cost doubles with every new module
Adding manpower to a late software project makes it later
Every program contains at least one defect per 1000 lines
exp: Brooks' law: adding people to a late project increases communication overhead and training effort, delaying it further.

q: A system has MTTF = 400 hours and MTTR = 20 hours. Its availability is approximately
exp: Availability = MTTF / (MTTF + MTTR) = 400/420 ≈ 0.952, i.e. about 95.2%.

q: Which UML diagram models the states of an object and the transitions triggered by events?
exp: State machine diagrams show an object's states and event-driven transitions. Class diagrams show static structure; component and deployment diagrams show physical organisation.

q: In the V-model of software development, acceptance testing is associated with which development phase?
exp: In the V-model each development phase is paired with a test level; user requirements correspond to acceptance testing.

q: Which technique describes requirements as sequences of interactions between a user and the system?
exp: A use case captures the dialogue between an actor and the system to achieve a goal.

q: In a UML class diagram, a line with a filled (solid) diamond at one end represents
exp: A filled diamond denotes composition (strong whole-part, part cannot exist without the whole); a hollow diamond denotes aggregation.

q: Mutation testing is used to
options: Evaluate the quality of a test suite by seeding small faults in the code
Convert black-box tests into white-box tests
exp: Small mutations are introduced into the program; a good test suite should detect (kill) the mutants.

q: In basic COCOMO for an organic project, development time is D = 2.5 × E^0.38 months. For an effort E = 32 person-months, D is approximately
In structured design, transform analysis and transaction analysis are used to convert:
options: a structure chart into source code
a data flow diagram into a structure chart
a use case into a class diagram
exp: Structured analysis produces DFDs; transform or transaction analysis maps the DFD to a structure chart (module hierarchy), the main structured-design output.

q: A test coverage analyzer reports
options: The response time of the application
The number of concurrent users supported
The percentage of code elements executed by the test suite
The defect density of the module
exp: Coverage tools instrument code and report which statements/branches were executed during testing.

q: A risk has a probability of occurrence of 0.3 and the loss if it occurs is Rs 2,00,000. The risk exposure is
exp: Risk exposure = probability × loss = 0.3 × 2,00,000 = Rs 60,000.

q: Level 5 (Optimizing) of the CMM is characterised by
exp: At the Optimizing level, quantitative feedback and innovative ideas drive continuous process improvement.

q: The application-composition model of COCOMO II estimates size using:
exp: COCOMO II application composition (used for prototyping and GUI-based projects) is based on object points; the early-design and post-architecture models use function points or SLOC.

q: According to the Agile Manifesto, which of the following is valued more?
options: Responding to change over following a plan
Following a plan over responding to change
Processes and tools over individuals and interactions
exp: The manifesto values responding to change over following a plan, while acknowledging value in the items on the right.

q: To unit test a module that calls other modules which are not yet developed, the tester uses:
exp: A stub is a dummy called module. A driver is a dummy calling module, used when the caller is missing.

q: Two modules communicate by reading and writing the same global data area. The type of coupling is
exp: Sharing global data between modules is common coupling.

q: Testing performed by the customer to decide whether to accept the delivered system is called
exp: Acceptance testing validates the system against user requirements and is used by the customer to accept or reject it.

q: A module has 45 defects found in 15 KLOC of code. The defect density is
exp: Defect density = 45 / 15 = 3 defects per KLOC.

q: Which combination of design characteristics makes software easiest to maintain?
options: Low coupling, high cohesion and good documentation
exp: Loosely coupled, cohesive and well-documented modules localize changes and are easy to understand.

q: Decision table testing is a technique of:
exp: Decision table testing derives test cases from combinations of input conditions in the specification, without looking at code, so it is black-box.

q: A Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) is
options: A chart of the team's organization
A hierarchical decomposition of project work into smaller tasks and deliverables
A table of costs versus benefits
exp: WBS breaks the project scope into manageable work packages in a tree structure.

q: Software Quality Assurance (SQA) activities are applied
options: Only to the final source code
exp: SQA is a process-wide umbrella activity covering reviews, standards, audits and testing at all phases.

q: Which of the following is a technique for requirements validation?
exp: Requirements validation checks that the SRS reflects customer needs using reviews, walkthroughs, prototyping and test-case generation.

q: Statement I: The Waterfall model easily accommodates changes in requirements late in development. Statement II: Prototyping helps in clarifying requirements. Which is correct?
options: Statement I is false and Statement II is true
Statement I is true and Statement II is false
exp: Waterfall is rigid and handles late change poorly, whereas prototypes elicit user feedback that clarifies requirements.

q: The IEEE 830 recommended practice deals with
exp: IEEE Std 830 gives recommended practice for writing an SRS.

q: Which tool shows the hierarchy of modules and the calling relationship between them?
exp: A structure chart depicts the modular hierarchy and the invocation relations among modules.

q: A program flow graph drawn as a planar graph has 6 regions (including the outer region). Its cyclomatic complexity is
exp: V(G) equals the number of regions of the planar flow graph, so V(G) = 6.

q: A team spends 20 person-months at a cost of Rs 50,000 per person-month and produces 10,000 LOC. The cost per LOC is
The cost of fixing a defect is generally lowest when the defect is detected during:
exp: The relative cost of correcting an error rises steeply with each later phase, so early reviews and inspections are the most economical.

q: A CASE tool that generates class skeleton code from a UML class diagram supports
exp: Generating code from design models is forward engineering; extracting models from code is reverse engineering.

q: Tasks: A (3 days, no predecessor), B (5 days, after A), C (2 days, after A), D (4 days, after both B and C). The minimum project duration is
exp: Longest path A→B→D = 3+5+4 = 12 days (A→C→D is only 9 days).

q: ISO 9001 is primarily concerned with
exp: ISO 9001 specifies requirements for a quality management system.

q: A major disadvantage of using Lines of Code (LOC) as a size metric is that it:
options: depends on language and programming style and is known accurately only after coding
ignores the cost of the project
exp: LOC varies with language and style, penalises concise code and is hard to estimate early; function points address this by measuring functionality.
